title: BLASPHEMERS & TRAITORS: JUDGE NOT BEFORE THE TIME

sense.text:
Blasphemy has levels. In its plainest sense it is expressing contempt, scorn or profound disrespect toward a deity, sacred things or religious beliefs: insulting speech, writing or actions directed at the divine. Under Moses the first level is plain: speak against the Lord and you die.

We came out of Egypt, and our sisters tended to mess around with the Egyptians. This was “the son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian”: an Israelite woman with a heathen child by an Egyptian man. He “strove together in the camp” with a man of Israel.

In that argument he “blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed.” Cursing here is not the f-word or a swear word. It means he spoke ill. Blaspheming and cursing are the same thing: insulting the divine.

His mother was “Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan”, a Danite sister.
“They put him in ward”: not inward, in ward, like a warden. They locked him up “that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them”, to find out what to do with him for talking like that.

“Bring forth him that hath cursed without the camp”, the one who cursed or blasphemed. Everyone who heard him lays hands on his head “and let all the congregation stone him.” He disrespected the Lord, so he is put to death.

“Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin.” Cursing his God and blaspheming the name of the Lord are one and the same. He was made an example to Israel: do what he did and you die the same as him.

“He that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death”, the stranger as well as the one born in the land. Blaspheme the Lord under Moses and it is an immediate death sentence.

Nathan comes to David with a story of two men in one city, a rich man with “exceeding many flocks and herds” and a poor man with nothing “save one little ewe lamb”, which grew up with his children and “was unto him as a daughter.” When a traveller came, the rich man would not take of his own flock but “took the poor man’s lamb.” A rich man robbed a poor man.

Nathan had to come at David this way. At this point David was out of his right mind, not in the spirit, and if Nathan had approached him plainly he would have killed him too. So he used an example to bring David to conviction.
David’s anger was kindled: “the man that hath done this thing shall surely die”, and “he shall restore the lamb fourfold”, because “he had no pity.”

“Thou art the man.” The rich man is David, and the poor man is Uriah the Hittite, whom David killed for his wife. The Lord had anointed him king, delivered him from Saul and given him his master’s house and wives, and would have given more. Yet David “hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword” (that is the poor man) “and hast taken his wife to be thy wife” (that is the ewe lamb).

David saw Uriah’s wife, liked her, lay with her and got her pregnant, then tried to get Uriah to go home so he would think the baby was his. When that failed he put Uriah in the hottest, most dangerous part of the battle and got him killed by the Ammonites.

“The sword shall never depart from thine house.” What David did secretly, the Lord brought on him publicly: “thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.”

After this David fell into one problem after another. One son raped his daughter; another son lay with his concubines and chased him out of his kingdom; his counsellor turned against him. His life was hell, and he was never the same.

David came to his senses: “I have sinned against the Lord.” He acknowledged it. And Nathan said, “The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.” The Lord had already forgiven him, but there would be evil in his house perpetually.

“By this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme.” It would get around that the king the Lord chose to replace Saul has men killed and takes their wives. David made the Lord look bad: he gave the enemies occasion to speak evil of God, to insult him, through David’s actions. That is another level of blasphemy, blasphemy brought on by what you do.

On top of that, “the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.” The Lord brought evil into David’s house.

Assyria was a rising empire conquering the nations around us, and saved the best for last. It destroyed the northern kingdom and came up against the southern kingdom in the reign of Hezekiah, a righteous king, so the Lord had his back; but when Assyria came near we were very fearful. Rab-shakeh was the ambassador of the Assyrian army, speaking for the king to get Judah to yield.

Eliakim, Shebna and Joah asked him to speak “in the Syrian language; for we understand it”, not in the Jews’ language in the ears of the people on the wall. The Assyrians and the Syrians are distinct peoples, but they intermingled and so did their languages. The Syrians are the children of Aram, Shemites, and the Syrian tongue is Aramaic. Through the migrations Aramaic slowly replaced the paleo-Hebrew we spoke.

Rab-shakeh answered that he was sent to the men on the wall, “that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you.” I’m not here to take your orders; I’m here to deliver a message, and I’ll make you drink your own piss and eat your own dung if I want to. In modern terms it means f you. This man was disrespectful.
So he “cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language”, so everybody would hear: “Let not Hezekiah deceive you”, and do not let him “make you trust in the Lord.” Don’t let your king lie to you.

“Make an agreement with me by a present”: pay your tribute and eat of your own vine and fig tree for now, “Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land.” Cooperate now, and when I come back I will deport you all out of your land and put our own people in it. But don’t let your king say your God is going to save you.

“Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered at all his land”? Did the gods of Hamath and Arpad and Sepharvaim stop us? Did they save Samaria? We conquered your brothers over there. Who are they “that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of mine hand?” Your God won’t save you either.

“The people held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king’s commandment was, saying, Answer him not.” We get loud, so the king said, don’t say nothing, let him talk. Then the king’s men came to Hezekiah “with their clothes rent”, mad, and told him the words of Rab-shakeh.

precepts.why:
Hezekiah “rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord”, and sent to Isaiah the prophet saying, “This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and blasphemy.” What was the blasphemy? Rab-shakeh saying your God won’t deliver you, your God ain’t going to save you, as if the Lord were like the gods of the other nations.

He was sent “to reproach the living God.” To reproach the living God is to blaspheme him. And the Lord’s answer by Isaiah: “Be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.”

This is the Lord’s answer to Rab-shakeh blaspheming him. “The virgin the daughter of Zion hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn”: you ain’t going to do nothing to us. “Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice”? Who do you think you are talking to? “Even against the Holy One of Israel.”

That is blasphemy: speaking against the Lord. The young man in Leviticus 24, the Egyptian’s child, did the same and was locked up and killed for it. The word was not used there, but cursing your God, reproaching the living God and blaspheming are the same thing.

All of Assyria’s victories and conquests were because of the Lord: “now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste fenced cities into ruinous heaps.” He made them an empire, and he knows “thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me.” He hears it all.

“Therefore I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.” The Assyrians were the most vicious, ferocious people, hated by many. They would put hooks in the noses of the people they conquered and drag them for miles out of their land, an ancient trail of tears; they did it to the northern kingdom. What you do to people, the Lord will do to you.

Watch how he turned Assyria back. Judas prays: “O Lord, when they that were sent from the king of the Assyrians blasphemed, thine angel went out, and smote an hundred fourscore and five thousand of them.” They were encamped outside Jerusalem, and one angel came down and killed 185,000. When those who survived woke up in the morning, all those men were dead.

Now go back home and carry your dead with you. Don’t play with the Most High. He sent one angel and killed 185,000; imagine two, three, four, five. All that blasphemy, all that talk Rab-shakeh did, went to nothing.

sense.text: The king sent Nicanor, “a man that bare deadly hate unto Israel”, who hated Israel with a passion, “with commandment to destroy the people.”

He sent to Judas “deceitfully with friendly words”: “Let there be no battle between me and you.” I just want to talk, no beef, I’ll bring a few men. That is Esau. But “the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by violence”: he was plotting on him. When Judas knew it, he would see his face no more.
Nicanor’s counsel was discovered, he got exposed, and he went out to fight Judas, and about five thousand of his men were slain. Judas was a fighter, a warrior.

Priests and elders came out of the sanctuary to salute him peaceably; the news of the beef between him and Judas had not reached them yet. “But he mocked them, and laughed at them, and abused them shamefully, and spake proudly.”
He swore that unless Judas were delivered into his hands, “I will burn up this house”: bring me Judas or I’ll burn this temple to the ground.

The priests stood before the altar weeping: “Be avenged of this man and his host, and let them fall by the sword: remember their blasphemies, and suffer them not to continue any longer.” We prayed for his death. We prayed, Lord, please kill this man for threatening to destroy your temple. We did not say, Lord, forgive him. That is white Jesus talk, Cesare Borgia talk.

precepts.why:
The same account told in more detail. Nicanor came into the temple and commanded the priests to deliver him Judas, and when they swore they could not tell where he was, “He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath”: “I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple unto Bacchus.” He would tear down the temple and set up another god in it.

The priests lifted up their hands to the Lord, “keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.” The unrighteous mouth is blasphemy.

The prayer was answered. Judas “commanded to strike off Nicanor’s head, and his hand with his shoulder”: his whole right arm, the one he stretched out against the temple. He brought them to Jerusalem “And shewed them vile Nicanor’s head, and the hand of that blasphemer, which with proud brags he had stretched out against the holy temple of the Almighty.”

“And when he had cut out the tongue of that ungodly Nicanor, he commanded that they should give it by pieces unto the fowls”: he talked that mess, so his tongue was cut out and fed to the birds, and his head and arm hung up before the temple for everyone to see. Judas Maccabeus was gangster. And every man praised the Lord: “Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled.”

sense.text: This is King Manasseh, king of Judah. He “seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel”: he convinced Jerusalem to do things worse than the nations we destroyed. Manasseh was the worst.

He “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did”, and the Amorites were terrible. Manasseh was a monster, and he “made Judah also to sin with his idols.”

Kings and Chronicles tell the same history: Kings gives more detail about the northern kingdom, and Chronicles more about the southern kingdom.

precepts.why:
The same account, written differently and in more detail. Manasseh made Judah “to do worse than the heathen.” The Lord spoke to him and his people, “but they would not hearken.” So the Lord brought the captains of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh “among the thorns”, among the wicked, “and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon”: into captivity.

“And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers”. That is where the Prayer of Manasses in the Apocrypha comes from. And the Lord “was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.”

After that he “took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the Lord”, cast the altars out of the city, “repaired the altar of the Lord”, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.

What he was doing: “he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. Those are ancient abortions: he burned his babies alive. “He observed times”, which is witchcraft and the zodiac, “and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards”. He was a witch, a sorcerer. And “he set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God”: he put an idol in the temple. He went crazy.

“Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another”: babies on babies, and the people did the same. That is a lot of blood. He was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft.

And the Lord forgave Manasseh. He humbled himself in his affliction, and the Lord put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy. Manasseh did evil far beyond what was worthy of death: he killed babies, went into witchcraft and defiled the temple, and the Lord said, I have mercy on you.

That is why humility matters. The Lord puts these things there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then from time to time, and that people fall and are able to rise again, like David. But all of us in here ain’t David, and you’re not Manasseh. Don’t abuse it. Don’t say, Moses got forgiven, so I can do it too. You ain’t Moses. That is pride. Humility.

sense.text:
They that were with Maccabeus laid siege to a fortress for four days, and the heathen inside, “trusting to the strength of the place”, were arrogant: you can’t get in here, your God ain’t going to do nothing. They “blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words.”

So blaspheming is uttering wicked words against the Lord. Cursing, reproaching and blaspheming are synonymous.
The Lord recalls to Ezekiel his dealings with us in the wilderness. He brought us out of Egypt, gave us his statutes and judgments, and “gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them”.

“But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness”: they walked not in his statutes, despised his judgments, “and my sabbaths they greatly polluted”, and he said he would pour out his fury upon them to consume them.

“But I wrought for my name’s sake”: he worked with us for his name’s sake. We represent him; we are his people, he named us, and his name is given to us. So the Lord tried to deal with us despite our rebellion, so that his name “should not be polluted before the heathen”.

He lifted up his hand that he would not bring them into the land, “which is the glory of all lands”: you are not worthy of it, you will die in the wilderness. That land is the best of all lands, the land they are fighting over to this very day; the war now is about obtaining all of it. Why? “Their heart went after their idols”, after other gods.

He lifted up his hand in the wilderness “that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries.” He warned us: I will scatter you to the four corners of the earth, put you in ships, make you exiles, a diaspora. We didn’t believe him. Their eyes “were after their fathers’ idols”: we followed our forefathers.

“Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live”: he judged us and was forced to kill us. “I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that openeth the womb”. The gifts were sacrifices, and the gifts were our own children, given to gods by being put in the fire and burned alive.

“Yet in this your fathers have blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me.” Going against the commandments, polluting his Sabbaths, killing our babies and serving other gods: that is blaspheming him, shaming him and defiling his name. By trespassing against him, we blasphemed him.

When he did give them the land, “they saw every high hill, and all the thick trees, and they offered there their sacrifices”. Even after finally gaining the land we still went into idolatry. “The provocation of their offering” means they pissed him off with sacrifices that made him angry. That was the blaspheming.

precepts.why:
“Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree”: the same high places Ezekiel names. Under every green tree is where we sacrificed our gifts, and our gifts were children. What do they do at Christmas? The gifts go right under the tree, an evergreen tree.

“And burn their groves with fire.” A grove is a stand of big trees. Today they call it the Bohemian Grove, with a big owl, where the presidents go, Obama included, with the trees high and tall around it and a fire. What goes in that fire? That is a grove where gifts are offered. The Lord said destroy that. That is blasphemy.

“Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, saith the Lord, which have burned incense upon the mountains, and blasphemed me upon the hills”. They blasphemed him by serving other gods upon the hills, the very thing the Lord forbade: “therefore will I measure their former work into their bosom.”

“My people is taken away for nought? they that rule over them make them to howl, saith the Lord; and my name continually every day is blasphemed.” Even now his name is blasphemed every day in wickedness. It does not mean people are saying his name wrong. It means his name and reputation are spoken evil of all around the world.

White Jesus is blasphemy. Saying he died for all people is blasphemy. Saying the gospel is for all people and all nations can be saved is blasphemy. Saying he ain’t the Son of God, saying he don’t exist, atheism, evolution: that is blasphemy.

sense.text: “Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old”: we are his congregation, his church. “The rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed”: redeemed means purchased again.
“All that the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary”. Here Asaph prophesies Babylon overthrowing Jerusalem.

“Thine enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations”: Babylon, and Rome as well, attacking us and killing us. “They set up their ensigns for signs.” Their ensigns for signs are Cesare Borgia, white Mary, baby white Jesus, white prophets, the Sistine Chapel, the Last Supper: posing themselves as God, the prophets, the angels and the heavenly Father, whitewashing our ensigns and making our signs their signs.
“A man was famous according as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees.” A man was once honored for cutting down trees, that was his skill, but now that same skill is used for idols.
“They have cast fire into thy sanctuary”, “they have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.” That is what Assyria and Babylon did.
“We see not our signs”: we don’t see our images. We don’t see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as a black man. We see their signs, their images, their depictions.
“Shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy. It is evil.
“The foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, and in some instances our own people, but primarily the nations.

precepts.why: On their ensigns for signs: Israel “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen painted their likeness into it: they made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain, Portugal, Britain, the Dutch and the French all did it, and they still do. That was blasphemy back then and it is blasphemy now.

sense.text:
“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty”: our works, our tribulation and our poverty, “(but thou art rich)” because we are God’s chosen people. “And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” They are Satan’s children.

Those who say they are Jews over there in Israel, in part of our land: that is blasphemy. Their feet on the land is blasphemy. The Muslims put a golden dome and a mosque there: blasphemy too. Both are guilty, the Palestinians and the Israelis; neither belongs there. The real Philistines, the Palestinians, we killed.

precepts.why:
“Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not”. The world is seeing it: the more evil they do, the more the world says those guys on the corners are right, these can’t be the people of God. They drop bombs on Iran, on Lebanon, on men, women and children in Gaza, and held a gay parade for four days in June in Israel, yet they are called the chosen people.

If you believe those are God’s people, that is blasphemy too. Accept them as God’s people or call them God’s people, and you blaspheme.

“A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: that is us: twelve stars, Israel, and the child she travails to deliver is Christ.

“A great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” A beast is a nation of people, and this red dragon is the so-called white man and the empires that come out of him, with his times of rulership. Show me red Japheth in the Bible. They say Isaac and Rebekah could not have a black child and a white child, yet they say Noah had Shem, Ham and a white Japheth. Noah could do it but Isaac couldn’t?

“And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world”. This is his fall: the downfall of the European power structure that controls the world, when Christ returns. No more white power. If you want it to last forever, that is blasphemy. He is that old serpent because he is the same serpent today that deceives the woman, especially the black and brown women, turning them against their men with feminism and dividing the Israelite families. He is Satan who calls himself a Jew today, and he deceives not just our people but the whole world. “His angels were cast out with him”: all his followers and allies.

The same red dragon in the same context: “there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months” over our people.

“He opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” His tabernacle: saying they belong in our land. Them that dwell in heaven: painting them as white, saying they don’t exist, calling them aliens, or calling them demons as JD Vance did recently. Those are angels up there, coming to save us and destroy them; so to him, yes, they are demons.

sense.text: “O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled”. This was prophesied in Psalm 74: they burned the sanctuary and made war against God’s people. Babylon did this. They gave the dead bodies of his servants to the fowls, shed their blood like water round about Jerusalem, and we became “a reproach to our neighbours”.
“Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee”: destroy the nations.

“Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is their God?” That is blasphemy. They conquered us and said, we are your god now. Where is your God? You are at the bottom of the ship. We are cutting your balls off and making you a eunuch, raping your wife and your daughter, turning your black woman against you, giving you crack cocaine, putting you in the ghettos and slums with redlining, hanging your child from a tree. Where is your God? Blasphemy.

“Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord, and their works are in the dark”. They do evil to us secretly: secret societies, the shadow government, the families that run the world, the oligarchs. “And they say, Who seeth us?” Black folks talk about the Illuminati; white folks don’t walk around saying they are Masons. They just do.

“Your turning of things upside down”: deceiving the world, as in Revelation 12. But the Lord will use his people to turn things right side up again.

“Shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not?” That is the atheist. “Or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?” That is, I’m a man, I should be a girl; I’m a girl, I should be a man. That comes to our people from the other nations, our environment and trauma at a young age, but it is still blasphemy: you are born one way and say God is wrong. Your organs tell you what you are. What woman can have prostate cancer? What man can have ovarian cancer? There are two genders.

“Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon”. Sit in the dust means fall, like Revelation 12, where the dragon is cast to the earth. “There is no throne”: your power is gone. “Thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”: the land of the free, the home of the brave.

“Thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly”. America dwells carelessly: she does what she wants to others and to her own people, passes laws secretly, raises prices, puts people in office who don’t belong there. And she “sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me”.

America gives people privilege and entitlement and makes her citizens care less, read less, think less. Our people cannot see a world without the white man ruling it; they say he has to be saved because negroes can’t rule over themselves. That is blasphemy, an insult to God: saying what God made can’t rule over itself. You are in hell trying to give your oppressor a heaven.

“I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children”: we will lose no citizens, we will not be defeated. That “I am” is blasphemy, from Babylon’s mouth and actions.

“But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood”: nuclear bombs, death. “They shall come upon thee in their perfection”: they will not miss; every missile will hit its target as God intends, “for the multitude of thy sorceries”.

“Thou hast said, None seeth me”, the same as Isaiah 29, working in the dark: the CIA, the FBI, the KGB, MI6, destabilizing countries and neutralizing leaders. “Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee”: they call it intel.

“Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels”: think tanks. “Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up”. There are prophets of God on the right hand and prophets of the devil on the left; Edom’s god is a devil, and he has prophets who speak in his favor. But “they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them”.

precepts.why: Where does Babylon get “I am, and none else beside me”? From God: “Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me”. Babylon says the exact same thing, putting herself in God’s place. America says, you’re a man, but if you want, I’ll make you a woman; you want to be a pedophile, come to this island. That is the blasphemy of “I am”.

sense.text:
The congregation wept and murmured against Moses and Aaron: “Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt!” “Were it not better for us to return into Egypt?” “Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.” Let’s go back to slavery. They got freedom and wanted to go back to massa because they were hungry. That is a slave mentality.

It is how we think now. I’m FBA, I’m from here, I’m indigenous. No, you were shipped here. This is not our home; this is exile, and we are here because we disobeyed our God. To pride yourself in America, I’m American, is blasphemy, because your home is Jerusalem.

precepts.why:
In the wilderness of Sin “the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron”: “Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots”, “for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

Murmuring, provoking the Lord, pissing him off, cursing Moses: the word is not used, but these are forms of blasphemy, speaking ill against the Lord, his people and his prophets.

“They sinned yet more against him by provoking the most High in the wilderness. And they tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust. Yea, they spake against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?” Is God capable of feeding us? That is blasphemy, reproaching God and his prophets Moses and Aaron, and they dropped dead in the wilderness for doing it.

sense.text: “An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes”: these are the elders and rulers with “the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.”

“Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself?” You preach a man should not steal; you should not be stealing, especially from your brothers in the body. You say a man should not commit adultery: is that what you are doing? “Thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?” Do you sacrifice to other gods?
“Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?” You boast that you keep the law; do you honor God by breaking it?

“For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you”. The leaders Paul was writing to were teaching and not doing. It is the same as the Lord telling David he gave the enemies occasion to blaspheme. Your actions can be blasphemy too, not only saying the name. Blasphemy has levels.

The Pharisees said, “This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.” They were saying Christ did his miracles with the power of Satan, casting out devils with the spirit of the chief devil. Keep that in mind.
“Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation”. If Satan casts out Satan, how does that benefit Satan? It is self-defeating and makes no sense.
“If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.”
“But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.” The kingdom of God is here, not the kingdom of Satan, meaning himself.

“All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.” Why did he say this? Because of what they said earlier. The Holy Ghost is the same Spirit of God in verse 28 that Christ used to heal the people, and they said that power was the devil. They were speaking evil of his power, blaspheming the spirit he used to heal people.

“Whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him”, against Christ himself, “but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost”, the power of Christ, what he was doing, “it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.”

precepts.why: “Whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.” Christ used the Spirit of God to heal the people, and they told people he did it by Satan.

The same account as Matthew 12; Mark, Peter’s scribe, gives more detail. The scribes from Jerusalem said, “He hath Beelzebub”. Christ asked, “How can Satan cast out Satan?” Why would Satan cast himself out?

“If a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand”: that is why we fell. “And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.” That is happening right now: America and Israel turning against each other, America burning bridges and going against NATO. Esau has an end.

“But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.” That is the difference. Ghost and spirit are the same thing; don’t let the words fool you. They said the Holy Spirit he used to heal people was an unclean spirit, that his power came from the devil and not from God. If they kept that mindset to death, that was it for them: condemned.

sense.text: Now to bring it to modern time. “As it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.” In Noah’s time the wicked ruled over the people and our people followed them, the same as today. “They did eat, they drank, they married wives”: we dwell carelessly in Babylon, until the flood came.

“Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot”: they bought, sold, planted and builded, life as usual, until fire and brimstone. Even so in the day the Son of man is revealed: everyone unsuspecting, living carelessly.

He on the housetop, let him not come down; he in the field, let him not return back: don’t look back when this place is destroyed, don’t miss it. “Remember Lot’s wife.” This place has an end. If you miss it, want to stay, think America will last forever, want to bring Babylon with you into the kingdom, that is your Lot’s wife: you are looking back because you are comfortable here. Noah and Lot were not comfortable.

Those who turn their backs on this truth are the same people who ignored Noah when the flood came and ignored Lot when the fire and brimstone came, and they will ignore us when Christ comes. It is the same mentality.

precepts.why:
“Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.” “Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.” That is cold: the hell with your family, they are all in the world. Some say that is a cult. No, Christ said, you follow me and do what I say: go preach the kingdom.

Another said, let me first go bid them farewell at home. “No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” Looking back like Lot’s wife. When you come to this truth there is no turning back, and many have looked back: put their hand to the plough and then said, this is a cult, I was brainwashed, now I’m free, and gone back to white Jesus. You saw brothers and sisters come in and change their lives, learn that Cesare Borgia is the fake image of Christ, that Christ is a black man, your God is black, the angels are black and the forefathers of the Bible are your forefathers, and then say, that’s a lie, we’re all one in Christ. That is blasphemy.

sense.text: “It is impossible for those who were once enlightened”: those who once learned the truth, “and have tasted of the heavenly gift”, the Holy Spirit that healed people in Matthew 12 and Mark 3, “and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, the very Holy Ghost Christ said not to blaspheme. “And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come”: they learned of Christ our king, the black messiah, arriving to deliver us out of this captivity, out of Babylon called America.

“If they shall fall away”, if you reject it, it is impossible “to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.” They kill Christ all over again: blasphemy. You put him to an open shame when you come out and say, that’s a cult, it don’t matter what color Christ is, I used to be a Hebrew Israelite, why I left IUIC.

We are not saying you can’t leave us. But when you turn around and say, I’m not a Hebrew Israelite no more, and you die in that, you are finished: a dead man or dead woman walking, going right into that fire.

precepts.why:
“If we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.” That is the hellfire waiting.

“He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”, like the man in Leviticus 24 who blasphemed, was put in ward and stoned. “Of how much sorer punishment”, then, for him “who hath trodden under foot the Son of God”: you crucify him afresh, you step on whatever you learned, take the purple shirt off and set it on fire on video. He “hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing”: now you say he died for everyone, and that defiles his death. He “hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace”: you came out of the world, learned who you are and got that grace, and now you are back in the church, baptized in the Christian church, back in the Catholic church, back at the mosque, back in the world. That Spirit of grace is the Holy Ghost you are blaspheming. This scripture explains blasphemy to the highest degree.

But “Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.” We can’t say you are condemned; that is the Lord’s decision. We can’t condemn Manasseh or David; the Lord had mercy on them, and they were worthy of death by the law of Moses for idolatry, adultery and murder. But if you die like that, never repenting, saying your God’s truth is a cult, it is over for you. “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” At the end of the day God has the say.

sense.text: “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” Many of our people come to this truth, join different camps, get offended and leave. But whatever camp you join or leave, it does not change what you are biologically. You can’t say, I used to be a Hebrew Israelite; that is like a Chinese man saying he is not Chinese anymore because he is mad at his mom and dad. You will always be a Hebrew Israelite. You just hate your people and your God now. You were dead in the world, you repented, and now you die again: a dead man squared.

precepts.why:
“Whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” We all make mistakes. A leader once said that a brother was disappointed in him when he came down, and it was the brother’s problem. No: that man looked up to you as a leader and you failed him, and you are held accountable because you offended him.

David offended his sons: his son raped his other son’s sister and David did nothing, because after killing Uriah he did not feel worthy to, and that affected his son. A leader who says, I fell, and if you’re mad about it that’s your business, is not a leader but a child pretending to be one, and should not be teaching at all. Christ said you should kill yourself: if you don’t repent of that offense, take a millstone and go into the river.

“It must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” Offenses will always come, but his offense causes the little ones to stumble, and he is held liable for it if he does not repent.

sense.text:
“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: that is why such a man will not hold himself accountable, because he loves himself. Look at my Prada, my Gucci, my gator shoes, a leader on IG arguing about whether Drake or Kendrick is the best rapper. These are elders? No, children.

“Blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: unthankful to those who came before them. They fell, but they built the foundation you walk on today, and you spit in their face. Disrespectful, shiftless, grimy.

They are “trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors”. There it is: traitors. I used to be a Hebrew Israelite, why I left. Why announce your departure? Just go. Nobody held you hostage or put a gun to your head. Wanting to be heard is emotional, feminine. But you are a traitor, going to the white man to say, I was there and I’ll tell you all the evil they were doing, when you saw all the good, and now all the good is evil.

Some who left are atheists now and come into the rooms trying to make others stop believing. If you no longer believe, don’t believe by yourself; why do we have to unbelieve too? Like a woman who comes in where women are working on themselves and says all men are bad: let them figure it out for themselves. Misery loves company. They want people to leave with them and die with them in the world. And when they leave they go right back to Christianity, the streets, Christmas, New Year’s and birthdays, and they get worse, never better. Outside of us, what are you in the Bible? Your family says welcome back, now we can all die together.

An elder who left said this is a movement, and movements stop. What we know as Israelites is wisdom, the truth of who we are. Wisdom has “an understanding spirit, holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good, quick, which cannot be letted”. Letted means it can’t be halted, it can’t be stopped. To say this movement will stop is not biblical; it comes from hurt, bitterness and anger. He fell, and it is hard to get up, but the Bible says it cannot be letted.

“For wisdom is more moving than any motion”: this is the top movement on the earth, despite how you feel. “She passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” If you are playing with the world, one foot in the Bible and one toe in the world, serving two masters, endorsing gang culture, messing with women, your movement stops, but the movement keeps going. That is why we travel the world, trying to find our people throughout the earth before Christ returns. Their line went out through all the earth: that is a movement.

“They have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love.” We have done right by a lot of people who left: helped with their mortgage and rent, helped get back children they lost, paid tuition so they could get their degree. Then they leave and give the middle finger.

“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That is why when they leave they are far worse than before they came in. They get a black line under their eyes; they are never the same.
“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Their prayers are not heard.
“Let his days be few; and let another take his office.” Who is this prophetically speaking of? All those shown who left are potentially that one, spiritually.

precepts.why: “Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents”. These scriptures say the same thing about the same kind of people.

“Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.” Those who left are familiar friends. Some raised their children among us: a child grows up from infancy to thirteen or fourteen among us, then you up and go, and the child’s friends are gone, because you are mad over something that could have been resolved easily, and you would not confront your own sin.

This happened to David with Ahithophel, his counsellor, who turned on him after what David did with Uriah. And it is also prophetic of somebody else.

“Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity”. This is Judas Iscariot. They paid him thirty pieces of silver to betray Christ; he felt bad and tried to give it back, and they said that is blood money, it can’t go back in the treasury, and bought a field with it. “And falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out”: he hanged himself and fell head first and burst open. His blood was spilled in the same field bought with the money used to betray Christ, “The field of blood.”

“For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.” He lost his position; he was replaced later in the same chapter by Matthias.

“I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.” That is the Psalm. Of the twelve, one was not chosen; one was chosen by the devil.

“None of them is lost, but the son of perdition”. The son of perdition is Judas, the betrayer. Did he blaspheme the Holy Ghost? Yes. How? When he realized what he had done, he did not go back and say, I repent. Out of guilt he ran and killed himself and never reconciled. Peter denied Christ and reconciled; Judas did not.

“But woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.” Woe means death and despair. He served his purpose, but he did not repent. Christ said leave your gift at the altar and go first to your brother; Judas did not do that. Killing yourself is not repentance; that is dying in your guilt.

So when you leave this body with things unresolved, say I’m no longer a Hebrew Israelite, why I left, and die like that, you are just like Judas, and you will suffer the same fate.

sense.text: “For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world”. We don’t go out and teach to condemn people. “But that the world through him might be saved.”
“He that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.”

“This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light”. Those that leave love darkness rather than light; this is too serious for them. One said, when I was there I learned to be a man, to be responsible, to pick a wife and be a father: what is the bad part? Many deal with secret sins, some with LGBT things; some brothers leave because their wives dominate them and they are scared of their women, and they call us a cult. No, brother, you are a victim; you left because of you, not because of us. One who left posted Christmas in front of a tree with his kids: that is what he wanted the whole time, the world. “Because their deeds were evil.”

“Every one that doeth evil hateth the light”: so the light becomes a cult, brainwashing, being bamboozled. “Lest his deeds should be reproved”: they don’t want correction. They despise dominion and government, so they leave.

“He that doeth truth cometh to the light”: they stay, “that his deeds may be made manifest”, whether good or bad, so they can be corrected, because we all make mistakes, “that they are wrought in God.”
“If by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead”: by any means, that I might get the kingdom.

“Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect”. Paul could not say he had made it. Some say, I’m the elect, I’m the 144,000. You don’t know that. Paul said he did not know. “If that I may apprehend”: that I may obtain the kingdom.

“I count not myself to have apprehended”: I have not obtained the kingdom yet; I am still here with you. “Forgetting those things which are behind”, putting the past behind me, “and reaching forth unto those things which are before”, working on myself now. “I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.”

Be mindful how you speak of the men who came before you. One who now calls the founder of his camp a false prophet is now looked at the same way himself. “Remember my judgment: for thine also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for thee.” When men fall and make mistakes, through coercion or old age as their wisdom leaves them, someone’s yesterday can be your tomorrow.

Do not speak evil of dignities, because the law will come and find you. Say Moses went off, the Baptist was a fake Israelite camp, James went off, Paul taught idolatry: the law will find you. Stay in your place. We learned from our elders to respect our elders; be careful to do the same, because yesterday for them, today for you.

“With me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment”. The Corinthians ran their mouths about Paul behind his back, and he said, I don’t care what you think about me. Paul had a past: he killed Christians, hunted us down like a bounty hunter, a madman, but the Lord called him out of that and he became a faithful servant. “Yea, I judge not mine own self”: I can’t say whether I am wicked or righteous.
“But he that judgeth me is the Lord.” That is all we say: if you die in that, that is on you.

“Therefore judge nothing before the time”, no one before the time, because what happened to me yesterday will happen to you today, “until the Lord come”. Then we will all know who made it and who didn’t. He “will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts”: in that day it will be known who was doing right, who was doing wrong, and who pretended. “And then shall every man have praise of God”: those who made it will have their praise of God.

precepts.why:
“Judge not, that ye be not judged.” Christianity’s favorite scripture. When you say someone blasphemed the Holy Ghost, you can’t make that call; it ain’t your call to make. You are out here blaspheming too, and you are going to the same place you say that person is going: saying he blasphemed the Holy Ghost while you mess with these hoes, endorse gang culture, get drunk at the bars every other week, rob women and rob your congregation to spend their hard-earned money on your clothes and debauchery.

“For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged”: with what you condemn, you will be condemned. “Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?” You say he blasphemed, while you blaspheme more and are still alive. “Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye”.

Luke explains what judge not means: “Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned”. To judge means to condemn; that is the precept of it. You cannot say someone is two-thirds, or that someone has blasphemed the Holy Ghost. That ain’t your place. Judge not before the time, because you might go to the same place they are going.

sense.text: “The unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God”: the same place blasphemers go, these go if they don’t repent. Fornicators: dating boyfriends and girlfriends, sleeping around. Idolaters. Adulterers, sleeping with someone’s wife or husband. Effeminate. “Abusers of themselves with mankind”: perverse acts, homosexual activity. Thieves, covetous, drunkards getting drunk every week. “Revilers”: those that speak evil of dignities and slander. “Extortioners”: those that extort and steal from a congregation. None of them “shall inherit the kingdom of God.”
“And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified”: if you stop. “But ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.”
“So fight I, not as one that beateth the air”: the truth is a fight. You are fighting your own battles, the sins of the world and the sins in yourself.

“But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”: that is how Paul fights; he has to fight himself all the time. We all have sins in us and a battle within us, so we can’t sit there and say he is condemned while we do the same thing or worse.

“Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway”: thrown back into the world. I’m no longer a Hebrew Israelite, why I left: if you stay that way, that is your call, and the Bible calls you a castaway.

Some told him of the Galileans “whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices”, killed while sacrificing. “Suppose ye that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans”? “I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” Christ would not call them the worst sinners.

The eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell: were they the biggest blasphemers of all time because the tower fell on them? “I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” You will die the same way.
A man had a fig tree in his vineyard that bore no fruit for three years: “cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?” It is a waste; get rid of it.

The dresser of the vineyard said, “Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it”: give it time, let me nourish it and prune it. “And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.”

We are all a work in progress. We all make mistakes, we may all fall at some point, but we must bring forth fruit meet for repentance. If you decide, I fell and I’m going to stay fallen, and give up on who you are, your God and your movement, you will be cut down. But God gives all of us a dispensation of time to get ourselves together. So we can’t condemn him or her for something we could just as easily be killed for; some of us have done worse. The same mercy the Lord had on David and on Manasseh can be extended to you.
